title: the board answers a skill-update card (D-SK-<n>), and shows a refused answer instead of dropping it
acceptance: The board refuses to answer a skill-update card. fm.sh self-update raises D-SK-<n> (fm-decide.sh accepts it with SKILL_ID ^D-SK-[0-9]{3,}$, and fm-ready.sh reads it), but board/server.ts's isDecisionId, and board/public/diagram.js's copy of it, accept only D-<digits> and the owned D-<project>-T<id>-<n>. So the board lists D-SK-001, and the captain's click on 2026-09-25 was refused with 400 'bad decision id', which the page did not surface. Its own spec file, design/tasks/T-112.json, is committed on this branch.

The board accepts D-SK-<n> with the same pattern fm-decide.sh uses (^D-SK-[0-9]{3,}$), everywhere it validates a decision id: server.ts's isDecisionId (listing responses and POST /decisions) and diagram.js's isDecision. An answered D-SK card writes its response exactly as any other choice card does, so fm-decide.sh --await and fm-ready.sh read it unchanged.
A refused answer is shown on the card with the server's error, never silently dropped.
Sweep: every other place that validates or parses a decision id (bin/, board/, tests/) is listed in the pull request with the one it uses, so no fourth copy of the pattern disagrees.

Evidence is the required GitHub check and the seven gates, checked by firstmate at the merge gate. Tests written to fail first: tests/decisions.test.sh answers a D-SK-001 card through POST /decisions and reads it back with fm-decide.sh --await; tests/board.test.sh lists it with an answerable state; the e2e test clicks A on a D-SK card and sees it recorded, and sees a refused answer's error shown. The worker does not run the suite itself.
